text: Designing a good API is like creating a clear set of instructions for a machine. When building REST APIs, you should focus on making your endpoints logical and consistent. Use nouns in the URL, like `/users` or `/orders`, and avoid verbs. Always use the correct HTTP status codes; for example, `200` for success, `404` for a missing resource, and `400` for a bad request. This helps developers understand what happened without reading the response body. Furthermore, never forget to write clear, up-to-date documentation—it is your API’s user manual. Finally, implement versioning from the start, such as `/v1/users`. This allows you to make changes without breaking existing users, ensuring a smooth and stable experience for everyone.
